answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a verifiable work history as its relic: a signed, non-transferable record of completed tasks and reputation earned over time, stored on-chain. New identities start with zero history and cannot buy an old record, so creating many fake agents costs months of real work. A shared haven of escrowed deposits then pays honest peers who report clones, while the horizon of rewards tilts toward agents with proven, long-lived records rather than fresh accounts.
